rules.name: Bucentaure (Rule 1)
rules.description: On top of its normal change of direction, the Bucentaure can make an additional change of direction during any part of its move.

rules.name: Bucentaure (Rule 2)
rules.description: A +1 modifier is added to all Skill Test rolls.

rules.name: Formidable
rules.description: As long as there are no more than one enemy ships of the line (3rd Rates of above) within 20" of the Formidable, she has +2 on all to hit rolls when aiming low.

rules.name: L'Orient (Rule 1)
rules.description: +1 To Hit when targeting British ships.

rules.name: L'Orient (Rule 2)
rules.description: When the L’Orient is on fire, it will always explode on an unmodified roll of 1 on the Skill Test to extinguish the flames, even if takes the +2 modifier (see page 26).

rules.name: Aiming High
rules.description: The French tended to shoot high to disable the opponent rather than sink it. therefore they only have -1 penalty for aiming high, instead of the normal -2. Additionally, if a Chain Shot is also loaded, the French suffer no penalty when aiming high.

rules.name: Streamlined
rules.description: French ships were usually very fast. The Streamlined Hull upgrade only costs 20 points for French ships as a result.

rules.name: Double Planking
rules.description: Some French ships were much sturdier than their counterparts. French ships may take the Sturdy upgrade for only 40 points.

rules.name: Admiral Pierre-Charles-Jean-Baptiste de Villeneuve
rules.description: Once per Turn, the ship captained by Villeneuve can make a Skill Test when receiving critical damage. A success means the critical damage is ignored.

rules.name: Captain Robert Surcouf
rules.description: The ship captained by Robert Surcouf has the Privateer upgrade at no extra cost. Furthermore the upgrade will also affect every ship in Surcouf’s fleet except those rated as between 1st and 4th rate.

rules.name: François-Paul Brueys d'Aigalliers (Rule 1)
rules.description: He provides a +1 to hit to the first broadside performed by his ship.

rules.name: François-Paul Brueys d'Aigalliers (Rule 2)
rules.description: Whilst François-Paul Brueys d'Aigalliers is alive, the ship he is on will not Strike the Colours, even if the Ship Points go below Break Value

rules.name: François-Paul Brueys d'Aigalliers (Rule 3)
rules.description: Every time the ship he is on takes a critical hit, roll a D10. On a result of 10 he is mortally wounded and his special rules cease to have effect.

rules.name: Charles René Magon de Médine (Rule 1)
rules.description: Magon's ship has a +1 to hit modifier against any British ship when aiming low.

rules.name: Charles René Magon de Médine (Rule 2)
rules.description: Magon's ship has a +1 modifier to all Skill Tests.

rules.name: Charles René Magon de Médine (Rule 3)
rules.description: Any ship Magon sails on must always follow the Rules of Engagement found on page 35 of the Black Seas rulebook, as well as the Awe and Fear rule on page 84 of the Hold Fast! book.

rules.name: Louis-Antoine-Cyprien Infernet (Rule 1)
rules.description: A ship that has Infernet on board will automatically pass the first three Break Tests it has to make.

rules.name: Louis-Antoine-Cyprien Infernet (Rule 2)
rules.description: When sailing with Light Sails, Infernet's ship may make an additional turn of up to 30-degrees (yellow) before its initial move.
